# Acnologia

> Acnologia is a self-hosted API key pool. It stores many API keys per provider (SerpAPI, ElevenLabs, Brave Search, Gemini, or any API key based HTTP service), hands out a working key on demand, detects rate limits, quota exhaustion and suspended accounts, cools keys down and rotates to the next one. Agents use it either as a proxy (Acnologia injects the key and the secret is never exposed) or by leasing a key and reporting the outcome.

Base URL is wherever Acnologia is deployed, for example `http://localhost:8080`. All consumer calls need an app token (`acn_...`) created in the dashboard. All bodies are JSON. Errors look like `{"error": {"code": "string", "message": "string"}}`.

Key facts for agents:

- Prefer proxy mode. Call `/proxy/{service}/{provider path}` exactly as you would call the provider, minus the provider key. Acnologia retries with the next key on rate limits.
- Use lease mode only when you must hold the raw key (for example a provider SDK). Always report the outcome so bad keys cool down and the key's concurrency slot is released.
- An app may be limited to some services and to mode `proxy`, `lease` or `both`. Call `GET /api/v1/services` to see what you can use.
- HTTP 503 `no_key_available`: every key is cooling down or exhausted. Wait `retry_after_sec` seconds.
- HTTP 503 `all_keys_busy`: usable keys exist but every one is at its concurrency limit or at a rate limit its provider publishes. Retry after `retry_after_sec` (usually 1) or lease with `wait_sec`.
- HTTP 503 `service_unavailable`: the provider keeps failing and its circuit breaker is open. Wait `retry_after_sec`.
- HTTP 429 `app_limit_reached`: your app used up its daily or monthly request or budget limit. `reset_at` says when it lifts.
- Report every lease within 10 minutes of `expires_at`. A second report gets 409, a late one 410.
- `{service}` can also be a service group: several services with the same API. Its strategy (priority, round_robin, random, cheapest or most_keys) picks the member that goes first and the rest are fallbacks. `X-Acnologia-Service` says which member answered.
- `{service}` can also be a capability: one job (such as searching places) that several providers do with APIs of their own. Call `/proxy/{capability}` with its params as query parameters or a JSON object body; Acnologia picks a provider by the strategy, translates the params into that provider's request, rotates its keys, and moves to the next provider on 401, 402, 403, 408, 429 or 5xx. Mapped routes answer `{items, count, capability, service, provider}` (or `{data, ...}`) in one shape whichever provider served. `_raw=1` returns the provider's own body; `_service=<slug>` pins one provider; `X-Acnologia-Tried` lists who was tried. `GET /api/v1/capabilities` lists them with their params, and each is one tool on `/mcp`.
- A service whose provider is `acnologia-peer` is shared by another Acnologia server: proxy only (leasing it gets 403 `lease_not_allowed`). 403 `share_revoked`, `share_paused` or `share_expired` means its owner revoked, paused or let it expire. 508 `loop_detected` means the request crossed more than 3 Acnologia servers.
- LLM APIs are built in providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Together AI, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI and more). Point an OpenAI compatible client at `/proxy/{service}/v1` with the app token as its API key.
- Acnologia never sends a key to Claude: requests from its own AI features pass a redactor, and keys pasted into its Assistant are vaulted.

## Auth

- `Authorization: Bearer acn_...` (preferred), or `X-Acnologia-Token: acn_...`.
- Proxy only: query parameter `?acn_token=acn_...` for tools that only accept a URL.
- Acnologia strips these before forwarding upstream.

## Consumer API

- [GET /api/v1/services](/llms-full.txt): services this token may use, with `available`, `base_url`, `auth` `{type, name, prefix}` and `guide_url`.
- [GET /api/v1/services/{slug}/guide](/llms-full.txt): how to call one service: endpoints, parameters, curl examples, limits and errors. Read it before calling a service you have not used. `?format=md` returns Markdown.
- [POST /api/v1/lease](/llms-full.txt): body `{"service": "serpapi", "exclude_key_ids": [], "ttl_sec": 300, "wait_sec": 0, "exclusive": false}`, returns `{"lease_id", "key_id", "service", "secret", "auth": {"type", "name", "prefix"}, "base_url", "expires_at"}` (put `prefix` before the secret when present), or 503 `no_key_available` / `all_keys_busy` with `retry_after_sec`.
- [POST /api/v1/leases/{lease_id}/report](/llms-full.txt): body `{"outcome", "status_code", "retry_after_sec", "message", "rotate"}`, returns `{"ok": true, "next": <lease or null>}`. With `rotate: true`, `next` is a fresh lease on another key.
- [POST /api/v1/leases/{lease_id}/renew](/llms-full.txt): body `{"ttl_sec"}`, returns `{"ok": true, "expires_at"}`.
- [ANY /proxy/{service}/{path}](/llms-full.txt): forwards to `base_url/{path}` with query string and body, injecting a key. Response headers add `X-Acnologia-Key-Id`, `X-Acnologia-Attempts`, `X-Acnologia-Service` and, with caching, `X-Acnologia-Cache`. Redirects are returned, not followed. Send `Cache-Control: no-cache` to skip the cache and `Idempotency-Key: <id>` to make retries safe for 10 minutes.
- [GET /healthz](/llms-full.txt): `{"ok": true, "version": "..."}`, no auth.

## Outcomes

- `ok`: call succeeded, resets the key's failure counter.
- `rate_limited`: key cools down for `retry_after_sec` (at most 24h), or exponential backoff from the service cooldown, capped at 1h.
- `busy`: the account is at its concurrency limit. The key steps aside for `retry_after_sec` (default 1s) without backoff.
- `quota_exhausted`: key parked as `exhausted` until its quota resets (or 24h).
- `invalid`: key marked `invalid` and removed from rotation until a health check passes.
- `banned`: the provider suspended the account. Only an admin reset brings it back.
- `error`: provider or network failure that is not the key's fault. The key is not penalized.

## Examples

- SerpAPI search: `GET /proxy/serpapi/search.json?engine=google&q=coffee` with `Authorization: Bearer acn_...`. Do not send `api_key`.
- ElevenLabs text to speech: `POST /proxy/elevenlabs/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}` with JSON `{"text": "Hello", "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2"}` and `Accept: audio/mpeg`. Do not send `xi-api-key`.
- The dashboard's Integrate tab has the same calls in curl, Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, C#, C++, Swift, Kotlin, PHP, Ruby and Dart.

## MCP

- [POST /mcp](/llms-full.txt): MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (JSON responses), same app token. Core tools: `list_services`, `pool_status`, `service_guide`, `get_key`, `renew_key`, `report_key`, `proxy_request`. Apps can also enable service tools generated from provider examples, read only insights (`list_keys`, `key_details`, `service_stats`) and key management (`check_keys`, `set_key_status`, `add_keys`). Stdio clients can run `acnologia mcp --url <base> --token acn_...`.
- [POST /mcp/control](/llms-full.txt): the control MCP, for running the server itself from an MCP client. It takes an admin API token (`acnadm_...`) and acts as its owner: services, keys, apps, providers, AI builds, sharing, usage and `call_service` (a provider call through the proxy). Destructive tools need `confirm: true`. Choose tools with `?groups=`, `exclude=`, `read_only=1`.

## SDKs

Twelve SDKs share one surface: proxy, lease, report with rotate, renew, an `exclusive` lease option, `with_key` (or `withKey`), typed errors including a busy error that still counts as "no key available" and a service unavailable error for an open circuit breaker, and `ACNOLOGIA_URL` / `ACNOLOGIA_TOKEN`. `with_key` always reports its leases. None is on a package registry yet: [SDKs](/docs/sdks.md) shows how to install each today.

- [Python](/llms-full.txt): `pip install acnologia`, then `from acnologia import Acnologia`.
- [TypeScript and JavaScript](/llms-full.txt): `npm install @acnologia/keys`, then `import { Acnologia } from "@acnologia/keys"`. Node 18+, Bun, Deno, browsers.
- [Go](/llms-full.txt): `go get github.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia/sdk/go`, package `acnologia`.
- [PHP](/llms-full.txt): `composer require acnologia/keys`, class `Acnologia\Acnologia`.
- [Ruby](/llms-full.txt): `gem install acnologia`, then `require "acnologia"` and `Acnologia::Client.new`.
- [Rust](/llms-full.txt): git dependency on crate `acnologia`, then `acnologia::Client::new`.
- [Java](/llms-full.txt): `dev.acnologia:acnologia`, class `dev.acnologia.Acnologia`. Java 17+.
- [Kotlin](/llms-full.txt): `dev.acnologia:acnologia-kotlin`, class `dev.acnologia.kotlin.Acnologia`, coroutines.
- [C#](/llms-full.txt): project `sdk/csharp/src/Acnologia`, class `Acnologia.AcnologiaClient`. .NET 8.
- [Swift](/llms-full.txt): `.package(url: "https://github.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia", branch: "main")`, `import Acnologia`.
- [Dart and Flutter](/llms-full.txt): git dependency with `path: sdk/dart`, `import 'package:acnologia/acnologia.dart'`.
- [C++](/llms-full.txt): CMake target `acnologia::acnologia`, `#include <acnologia/acnologia.hpp>`. C++17 and libcurl.

## Admin API and CLI

Operators can script the admin API with a token from Account, API tokens (`Authorization: Bearer acnadm_...`, scope `read`, `write` or `admin`, never above the creator's role). The `acn` CLI (`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia/main/install.sh | sh`, on Windows `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia/main/install.ps1 | iex`, also built in as `acnologia ctl`) signs in through the browser with `acn login`, or takes a token with `acn login https://keys.example.com --token acnadm_...`; then `acn status`, `services`, `keys <service>`, `keys add <service> < keys.txt`, `keys check <service>`, `events`, `breaker <service> [--reset]`, `cache purge <service>`, `usage <app-id>`.

## Docs

Every page of the docs is also served as raw Markdown. Fetch these when you need detail beyond the consumer API.

- [Overview](/docs/overview.md): what Acnologia does, quick start and features.
- [HTTP API](/docs/api.md): consumer error codes and every dashboard route with its required role.
- [Command line](/docs/cli.md): install the acn CLI, sign in through the browser, commands and CI variables.
- [SDKs](/docs/sdks.md): the seventeen client libraries, how to install each today, the shared surface and running their tests.
- [Configuration](/docs/configuration.md): environment variables, per service settings, self-hosting, Windows, the access password, backups and upgrading.
- [Deploying](/docs/deploy.md): every deploy option, one click on Render or Railway, Fly.io, the container image and the settings a public deploy needs.
- [Deploying on Railway](/docs/deploy-railway.md): a public deploy behind the access password, with a volume, AI and sharing.
- [Deploying on a server](/docs/deploy-vps.md): one script for any Linux server with HTTPS, cloud-init, Hetzner and DigitalOcean.
